newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-No submarine decision likely before end year - McLachlan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-No submarine decision likely before end year - McLachlan.

text.p: Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said on Friday a decision on whether the Royal Australian Navy might purchase two additional Collins class submarines did not have to be made until the end of this year.

Speaking at the launch of the third of six submarines being built for the navy in a A$5.3 billion contract by the Australian Submarine Corp, McLachlan said the defence department had to consider a number of competing procurement possibilities.

"We have a quite limited budget, I would personally like it to be more but that is not going to be the case and quite frankly those decisions simply cannot be made until towards the end of this year," he told journalists.
Under the contract, the navy has the option for another two submarines to be constructed.
McLachlan said the government still hoped the ASC would be able to win submarine orders from third parties, but he believed it may be some time before any orders would come through.
"Obviously back in the 1980s people did not decide to build submarines in Australia on the basis it was a one-off," he said.

The first of the submarine fleet, HMAS Collins is now based with the navy in Perth, the second, the Farncomb will be officially handed over to the navy later this year, while the third, the Waller, now will begin technical testing ahead of sea trials.
